'''Doug Taylor''' was a [[Players Committee]] advocate from 2002, serving later as [[Design Advocate]] and [[Historical Advocate]].<ref name="pc1" /><ref name="home2002" /><ref name="vol2009b" /> Warren Holland named him and Eric Olson the first Player Advocates for Gameplay Support on 25 January 2002.<ref name="pc1" /> Before that he was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Red 4 FL from Lynnwood, Wa. The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run. [[Winfried Sommerfeld]] (Red 41) named him among the friends he made through Star Wars CCG.<ref name="decsq-sommerfeld">[http://decipher.com/volunteers/squadrons/players/sommerfeldwinfried.html Star Wars CCG Squadrons: Red 41], decipher.com (page last modified 28 June 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001023104822/http://decipher.com:80/volunteers/squadrons/players/sommerfeldwinfried.html Internet Archive]</ref>

On his third tour as a Squadron Member, he built a Seattle-area list of nearly 300 players. One of his Regional qualifiers drew 91 players, then a world record.<ref name="decsq-prof" />

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables.

== Jedi Knights TCG ==
Taylor playtested the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref> As a Decipher Product Champion volunteer he reported on a Seattle pre-release event with about 40 players in April 2001.<ref name="jkprerelease">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/articles/042701storyC.html Pre-Release Parties Launch Jedi Knights!], decipher.com (April 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010910003958/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/articles/042701storyC.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Radio Free Decipher (2002) ==
On ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' Broadcast 112 (25 January 2002), host [[Kyle Heuer]] described Taylor as a Seattle-based, long-time Decipher playtester. He would do design for the [[Players Committee]] with [[Eric Olson]]. Heuer said Taylor wanted storyline and an element of fun incorporated into cards, balancing Olson's numbers-driven approach.<ref name="rfd112">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=docK2vpQWUI&t=1043s Broadcast 112 - Radio Free Decipher (25 January, 2002): Scott Gaeta on the SWCCG PC], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 17:23. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-docK2vpQWUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 112 transcript]].</ref>
